bottleneck: Huntington's disease requires silencing only the mutant huntingtin allele while sparing the healthy one, since total huntingtin loss is itself harmful to neurons. Allele-specific targeting depends on heterozygous SNPs that differ between patients, demanding personalized guides for each individual, and the CAG repeat itself is a poor CRISPR target because repeats confuse guide specificity. Delivery must also reach the striatum's vulnerable neurons at therapeutic levels without harming cortex.
current_state: Non-selective huntingtin-lowering trials reduced both alleles and showed safety signals; allele-specific approaches are in early clinical testing with patient-specific designs.

title: Huntington's needs allele-specific silencing we lack
why_it_blocks: A therapy that silences the good copy along with the bad trades one neurodegeneration for another. Precision at the allele level is the whole game in Huntington's, and the field is still learning to play it.
